Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: During the 9th century, southern Central Asia was ruled by the Samanids, while the Central Asian steppe was dominated by Turkic nomads such as the Pechenegs, the Oghuz Turks, and the Karluks.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The Karluk center in the 9th and 10th centuries appears to have been at _____ on the Chu

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: In the late 9th century, the _____ marched into the steppes and captured Taraz, one of the headquarters of the Karluk khagan, and a large church was transformed into a mosque
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: In the late 9th century, the Samanids marched into the steppes and captured Taraz, one of the headquarters of the Karluk khagan, and a large church was transformed into a mosque.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The Chigils appear to have formed the nucleus of the _____ army
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The Chigils appear to have formed the nucleus of the Karakhanid army. The date of its foundation and the name of its first khan is uncertain, but according to one reconstruction, the first Karakhanid ruler was Bilge Kul Qadir Khan.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The date of its foundation and the name of its first khan is uncertain, but according to one reconstruction, the first Karakhanid ruler was _____
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The date of its foundation and the name of its first khan is uncertain, but according to one reconstruction, the first Karakhanid ruler was Bilge Kul Qadir Khan.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The names of animals were a regular element in the Turkic titles of the _____: thus Aslan (lion), Bughra (camel), Toghan (falcon), Böri (wolf), and Toghrul or Toghrïl (a bird of prey)
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The rulers of the Karakhanids were likely to be from the Chigil and Yaghma tribes – the Eastern Khagan bore the title Arslan Qara Khaqan (Arslan "lion" was the totem of the Chigil) and the Western Khagan the title Bughra Qara Khaqan (Bughra "male camel" was the totem of the Yaghma). The names of animals were a regular element in the Turkic titles of the Karakhanids: thus Aslan (lion), Bughra (camel), Toghan (falcon), Böri (wolf), and Toghrul or Toghrïl (a bird of prey).

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: Under the _____ were four rulers with the titles Arslan Ilig, Bughra Ilig, Arslan Tegin and Bughra Tegin
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: Under the Khagans were four rulers with the titles Arslan Ilig, Bughra Ilig, Arslan Tegin and Bughra Tegin.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: Later they adopted the Arab titles sultan and sultān al-salātīn ("Sultan of _____")
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: Later they adopted the Arab titles sultan and sultān al-salātīn ("Sultan of Sultans").

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: According to the _____ historian known as Munajjim-bashi, a Karakhanid prince named Sultan Satuq Bughra Khan was the first of the khans to convert
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: According to the Ottoman historian called Munajjim-bashi, a Karakhanid prince named Sultan Satuq Bughra Khan was the first of the khans to convert.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The Eastern Khanate ended in 1211, and the _____ was extinguished by the Khwarazmian Empire in 1212
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The Khanate split into the Eastern and Western Khanates in the 1040s. The Eastern Khanate ended in 1211, and the Western Khanate was extinguished by the Khwarazmian Empire in 1212.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: In the late 11th century, they came under the suzerainty of the _____ followed by the Qara Khitai (Western Liao dynasty) who defeated the Seljuks in the Battle of Qatwan in 1141
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: In the late 11th century, they came under the suzerainty of the Seljuk Empire followed by the Qara Khitai (Western Liao dynasty) who defeated the Seljuks in the Battle of Qatwan in 1141.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The Khanate conquered _____ in Central Asia and ruled it independently between 999 and 1089
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The Khanate conquered Transoxiana in Central Asia and ruled it independently between 999 and 1089. Their arrival in Transoxiana signaled a definitive shift from Iranic to Turkic predominance in Central Asia, yet the Kara-khanids gradually assimilated the Perso-Arab Muslim culture, while retaining some of their native Turkic culture.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: In _____, the Karluks were part of an alliance led by the Basmyls and the Uyghur Khaganate that rebelled against the Göktürks, leading to the demise of the Second Turkic Khaganate (682–744)
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: In 742, the Karluks were part of an alliance led by the Basmyls and the Uyghur Khaganate that rebelled against the Göktürks, leading to the demise of the Second Turkic Khaganate (682–744).

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: After conversion, he obtained a fatwa which permitted him in effect to kill his presumably-still-pagan father, after which he conquered Kashgar (of the old _____)
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: After conversion, he obtained a fatwa which permitted him in effect to kill his presumably-still-pagan father, after which he conquered Kashgar (of the old Shule Kingdom).

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: According to the Ottoman historian called Munajjim-bashi, a Karakhanid prince named Sultan Satuq Bughra Khan was the first of the khans to convert. Sulayman (or Harun) (title: Bughra Khan) attacked the Samanids in the late 10th century.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: Between 990 and 992, Hasan took _____, Ferghana, Ilaq, Samarkand, and the Samanid capital Bukhara
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: Between 990 and 992, Hasan took Isfijab, Ferghana, Ilaq, Samarkand, and the Samanid capital Bukhara.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: However, _____ died in 992 due to an illness, and the Samanids returned to Bukhara
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: However, Hasan Bughra Khan died in 992 due to an illness, and the Samanids returned to Bukhara.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: Musa (title: _____ or Arslan Khan) resumed the campaign against the Samanids, and by 999 Ali's son Nasr had taken Chach, Samarkand, and Bukhara
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: Musa (title: Kara Khan or Arslan Khan) resumed the campaign against the Samanids, and by 999 Ali's son Nasr had taken Chach, Samarkand, and Bukhara.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The Samanid domains were divided between the _____, who gained Khorasan and Afghanistan, and the Karakhanids, who received Transoxiana
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The Samanid domains were divided between the Ghaznavids, who gained Khorasan and Afghanistan, and the Karakhanids, who received Transoxiana.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The Karakhanid state was divided into appanages (Ülüş system), as was common of _____ and Mongol nomads
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The Karakhanid state was divided into appanages (Ülüş system), as was common of Turkic and Mongol nomads.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The dynasty's original domains of _____ and Kasgar and their khans retained an implicit seniority over those who ruled in Transoxiana and Fergana

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

The dynasty's original domains of Zhetysu and Kasgar and their khans retained an implicit seniority over those who ruled in Transoxiana and Fergana.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: Ahmad was succeeded by _____, and after the death of Mansur, the Hasan Bughra Khan branch of the Karakhanids became dominant

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The two families, i.e., the descendants of Ali Arslan Khan and Hasan Bughra Khan, would eventually split the _____ in two

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: In _____–1018, the Karakhanids repelled an attack by a large mass of nomadic Turkic tribes in what was described in Muslim sources as a great victory
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: In 1017–1018, the Karakhanids repelled an attack by a large mass of nomadic Turkic tribes in what was described in Muslim sources as a great victory.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The Qara Khitai themselves stayed at Zhetysu near Balasagun, and allowed some of the Karakhanids to continue to rule as their tax collectors in Samarkand and Kashgar.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kodak 35 Rangefinder.question: The Kodak _____ Rangefinder is an improved version of the Kodak 35 that was launched by the Eastman Kodak Company in 1938 as their first 35mm camera manufactured in the USA
Kodak 35 Rangefinder.fact: The Kodak 35 Rangefinder is an improved version of the Kodak 35 that was launched by the Eastman Kodak Company in 1938 as their first 35mm camera manufactured in the USA. After some two years, the Company presented this improved Kodak 35 camera, with a new superstructure housing containing a viewfinder and a separate rangefinder, but without any addition to the identifying inscription on the body.
